newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB'S KAHN TAKES POLICE JOB FOR TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SAB'S KAHN TAKES POLICE JOB FOR TWO YEARS.

text.p: South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) group chairman Meyer Kahn has accepted a two-year secondment to a new top civilian position in the country's police force to help fight crime, the company said on Saturday.
Former African National Congress (ANC) politician Cyril Ramaphosa will be the SAB board's acting non-executive chairman while Kahn, who takes up the job on August 1, is away, SAB said.

Kahn is to become the chief executive of the South African Police Service (SAPS) -- "a new civilian function calculated to direct and accelerate the conversion of SAPS into an effective law enforcement and crime prevention agency", SAB said.
"Mr Kahn has agreed to accept this responsibility and the SAB board accordingly approved his secondment to government for two years," the statement said.

It said SAB deputy chairman Selwyn MacFarlane would become acting chairman of the board's general purposes committee and group managing director Graham Mackay would assume full executive responsibility.

Kahn has been instrumental in building SAB up into one of South Africa's top five corporations, and promoting its push into African, east European and other overseas markets, especially since the demise of apartheid in 1994.
